Vehicle and Cargo Declaration Submission: This legal instrument is formally titled the Vehicle and Cargo Declaration Submission and Pre-arrival Processing Rules 2025.
The rules apply to all imports, transit shipments, and the arrival of crew and passengers from abroad.
These rules shall come into force thirty days after the date of their official issuance.

Customs Act 2023: The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 2023 for the purposes of these rules.
Authorized Person or Agent: The term Agent is defined with reference to the specific definition provided under the Customs Act 2023.
Cargo Declaration: The term Cargo Declaration is defined by referencing the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: The term Customs Computer System is defined by referencing the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.
Dangerous Goods: Dangerous Goods refers to all products classified under the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code and the International Air Transport Association (IATA) Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR).
Person in Charge of Conveyance: A Vehicle or Cargo Declarant is defined as the person in charge of a conveyance, or their owner, operator, or agent, who is responsible for filing declarations and holds registered credentials for the Customs Computerised Entry Processing System.
Shipping Agent: A Shipping Agent is defined as any person, entity, or organization managing business related to the arrival, stay, or departure of a conveyance, including local representatives of foreign shipping lines.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
৩। বাংলাদেশে আগমনকারী যানবাহনের কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিল পদ্ধতি।─ (১) বাংলাদেশের বাহির হইতে বাংলাদেশে আগমন করিবে এইরূপ সকল যানবাহনের ক্ষেত্রে বাংলাদেশে আগমনের উদ্দেশ্যে বিদেশস্থ সর্বশেষ বন্দর ত্যাগের পূর্বেই কার্গো ঘোষণাকারী কর্তৃক ইলেকট্রনিক পদ্ধতিতে কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমে পরিশিষ্ট-১ এ বর্ণিত ফরমে কার্গো ঘোষণার প্রথম অংশ দাখিল করিতে হইবে, যাহা জেনারেল সেগমেন্ট (General segment) হিসেবে বিবেচ্য হইবে; এবং তৎপরবর্তীতে উক্তরূপ তথ্যের সহিত সামঞ্জস্য রাখিয়া পরিশিষ্ট-২ অনুযায়ী ওয়েববিল সেগমেন্ট (Waybill segment) এবং পরিশিষ্ট-৩ অনুযায়ী কন্টেইনার বা কনসাইনমেন্ট সেগমেন্ট (প্রযোজ্য ক্ষেত্রে) এ তথ্য দাখিল করিতে হইবে:

ততবে শর্ত থাকে যে, বাল্ক কার্গো, স্ক্র্যাপ জাহাজ এবং অয়েল ট্যাঙ্কারের মাধ্যমে পণ্য আমদানির ক্ষেত্রে জাহাজ বা নৌযান বাংলাদেশে আগমনের পরবর্তী ২৪ ঘণ্টার মধ্যে কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিল করা যাইবে।

(২) কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে উক্ত পণ্যচালান সংশ্লিষ্ট বিল অব লেডিং অথবা এয়ারওয়ে বিল অথবা ট্রাক রিসিপ্ট অথবা রেলওয়ে রিসিপ্ট, যেই ক্ষেত্রে যেইটি প্রযোজ্য এবং এতদসংশ্লিষ্ট দলিলাদির ভিত্তিতে কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিল করিতে হইবে।

(৩) বোর্ড কার্গো ঘোষণাকারীর নিজস্ব ইলেকট্রনিক সিস্টেমের সহিত কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমের আন্তঃসংযোগ স্থাপনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করিতে পারিবে এবং উক্ত সংযোগের মাধ্যমে কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমে সরাসরি কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিল করিবার অনুমতি প্রদান করিতে পারিবে।

(৪) এই বিধির অন্যান্য বিধানে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, অনিবার্য কোনো কারণে কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমে কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিল করা সম্ভব না হইলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস বা সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশনের দপ্তর প্রধান এর লিখিত অনুমতি ক্রমে কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমে দাখিলতব্য কার্গো ঘোষণার অনুরূপ তথ্য পরিবেশন করিয়া লিখিত বা মুদ্রিত কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিল করা যাইবে।

Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: Cargo declarations must be submitted electronically to the customs system prior to the departure of a vessel from its final foreign port of call.
The system facilitates the submission of cargo declarations in segments including general, waybill, and container or consignment segments.
The National Board of Revenue may permit the direct integration of a declarant's internal electronic system with this system for automated filing.

In cases of technical failure or unavoidable circumstances preventing electronic submission, the system allows for the manual filing of cargo declarations upon written authorization from the Commissioner of Customs or the head of the customs station.
Cargo Declaration: All vessels entering Bangladesh must submit cargo declarations comprising specific segments such as the general segment, waybill segment, and, where applicable, the container or consignment segment.
Declarations must be prepared based on relevant transport documents such as bills of lading, airway bills, truck receipts, or railway receipts.
Bulk cargo, scrap vessels, and oil tankers are granted a grace period allowing the submission of cargo declarations within twenty-four hours after arrival in Bangladesh.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to establish interconnections between the electronic systems of cargo declarants and the official customs computer system to streamline the declaration process.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner or the head of a customs station has the authority to grant written permission for the submission of manual or printed cargo declarations when electronic filing is not possible due to unavoidable circumstances.

৪। বাংলাদেশে আগমনকারী যানবাহনের ক্রু ও যাত্রী ঘোষণা পদ্ধতি।─ (১) বাংলাদেশের বাহির হইতে বাংলাদেশে আগমন করিবে এইরূপ সকল যানবাহনের ক্ষেত্রে যানবাহনের ক্রু ও যাত্রীর বিবরণ সম্বলিত ঘোষণা তথা, আইনের ধারা ৪৮(৩) এ উল্লেখিত অ্যাডভান্স প্যাসেঞ্জার ইনফরমেশন (API) এবং প্যাসেঞ্জার নেইম রেকর্ড (PNR) বিদেশস্থ সর্বশেষ বন্দর ত্যাগের পূর্বেই যানবাহন বা কার্গো ঘোষণাকারী কর্তৃক কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমে দাখিল করিতে হইবে:

তদবে শর্ত থাকে যে, উল্লিখিত ঘোষণা কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমে অনিবার্য কোনো কারণে দাখিল করা সম্ভব না হইলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস বা সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশনের দপ্তর প্রধান এর অনুমতি ক্রমে একই তথ্য সম্বলিত ঘোষণা লিখিত বা মুদ্রিত দাখিল করা যাইবে:

আরও শর্ত থাকে যে, স্থলপথে আগমনকারী যানবাহনের ক্ষেত্রে সংশ্লিষ্ট কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস বা সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশনের দপ্তর প্রধান আদেশ জারির মাধ্যমে যানবাহনের আগমনের পরে ক্রু ও যাত্রী ঘোষণা দাখিলের সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে।

(২) উপ-বিধি (১) এ যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, স্থলপথে পণ্যবাহী যানবাহন আগমন ও প্রস্থানের পূর্বে যথাযথ কাস্টমস কর্মকর্তার নিকট ‘ফরম-ক’ অনুসারে কার পাস দাখিল করিয়া উহাতে যানবাহন ও ক্রু আগমনের অনুমতি গ্রহণ করিতে হইবে:

তদবে শর্ত থাকে যে, শুধু যাত্রী বহন করিয়া থাকে এইরূপ যানবাহনের ক্ষেত্রে কার পাস দাখিলের বিধান প্রযোজ্য হইবে না।

(৩) সংশ্লিষ্ট কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস বা সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশনের দপ্তর প্রধান ইলেকট্রনিক পদ্ধতিতে কার পাস দাখিল করিবার আদেশ জারি করিতে পারিবে এবং উক্ত আদেশ অনুসারে স্থলপথে আগমনকারী যানবাহনের ক্ষেত্রে ইলেকট্রনিক পদ্ধতিতে কার পাস দাখিল করা যাইবে।

Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: Vehicle or cargo declarants must submit Advance Passenger Information and Passenger Name Record to this system before departing the final foreign port for Bangladesh.
In cases of unavoidable system failure, the Commissioner of Customs or head of the customs station may authorize the submission of such declarations in written or printed format.
Advance Passenger Information (API): This information is required under the Customs Act for all incoming vehicles, crews, and passengers to be submitted via the designated customs system prior to arrival.
Passenger Name Record (PNR): The PNR is a mandatory declaration component for crews and passengers of vehicles arriving in Bangladesh from abroad, to be filed through the customs computer system before departure from the last foreign port.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner or head of the customs station holds the authority to permit alternative submission methods if electronic filing is unavailable and may issue orders allowing post-arrival declaration for land-based transport.
They have the authority to mandate the electronic submission of Car Passes for land vehicles.
Car Pass: For goods-carrying vehicles entering or exiting by land, a Car Pass in the prescribed format must be submitted to the appropriate customs officer to obtain authorization for vehicle and crew movement.
The requirement for a Car Pass does not apply to vehicles used exclusively for passenger transport.
Customs Act 1969: This Act serves as the primary legislation governing the declaration requirements for passengers and crews of vehicles entering Bangladesh, specifically referencing the submission of Advance Passenger Information.

Transit and Transshipment: The declaration of vehicles or cargo during transit or transshipment operations must comply with the terms stipulated in the relevant transit or transshipment agreement.
Such declarations are to be executed in accordance with orders issued by the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to issue orders that define the specific requirements for declaring vehicles or cargo undergoing transit or transshipment.

(২) উপ-বিধি (১) এর টেবিলের ক্রমিক ৫ এ উল্লিখিত স্থলপথে আগমনকারী যানবাহনের ক্ষেত্রে যানাবাহনের ভারপ্রাপ্ত ব্যক্তি (person-in-charge) অথবা তাহার পক্ষে উক্ত যানবাহনের মালিক বা পরিচালনাকারী কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিলের জন্য ‘ফরম-খ’ অনুসারে কোনো এজেন্টকে দায়িত্ব অর্পণ করিতে পারিবে।

(৩) উপবিধি (১) ও (২) এ যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, বোর্ড আদেশ জারির মাধ্যমে কোনো নির্দিষ্ট রুট বা কাস্টমস স্টেশনে উপবিধি (১) এর টেবিলের কলাম (৩) উল্লিখিত কার্গো ঘোষণাকারী পরিবর্তন করিতে পারিবে অথবা অন্য কাউকেও কার্গো ঘোষণাকারী হিসেবে নির্ধারণ করিতে পারিবে।

Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a vessel, aircraft, or vehicle arriving from abroad is responsible for submitting cargo declarations based on the specific route taken.

They may designate agents or freight forwarders to act on their behalf for cargo declarations, or in the case of land routes, they may perform these functions themselves subject to obtaining specific licensing requirements.
Freight Forwarders: Freight forwarders are formally recognized as authorized entities to submit cargo declarations for sea and inland water transport routes when designated by the owner, operator, or the person in charge of the vessel.
National Board of Revenue: The board holds the authority to issue orders modifying or designating alternative parties as cargo declarants for specific routes or customs stations, regardless of the default rules prescribed for vehicle and cargo declaration.
Customs Act 1969: The licensing of agents for land transport cargo declarations is governed by provisions established under the authority of Section 243 of the Act.
Bangladesh Railway: For cargo arriving directly from abroad by rail, the designated official of the Bangladesh Railway is responsible for submitting the necessary cargo declarations.

Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: This system is designated for the submission of vehicle or cargo declarations by licensed individuals.
Users are required to be registered and follow prescribed procedures to obtain the necessary credentials for system access.
Customs Act 1969: Section 243 of the Act provides the authority for the licensing of individuals to interact with customs processes and systems.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৮। বিপজ্জনক পণ্য (Dangerous Goods) এর ক্ষেত্রে ওয়েবিল ঘোষণা প্রদান।─ আমদানিযোগ্য পণ্যের মধ্যে কোনো বিপজ্জনক পণ্য (Dangerous Goods) থাকিলে ওয়েবিল সেগমেন্ট দাখিল করিবার সময় সংশ্লিষ্ট কার্গো ঘোষণাকারী পরিশিষ্ট-৪ অনুযায়ী DG Status এর ঘরে ঘোষণা প্রদান করিবে।

Dangerous Goods: The person declaring the cargo must provide a specific declaration for dangerous goods during the submission of the waybill segment. This declaration is to be made by indicating the dangerous goods status in the relevant designated field as specified in the relevant regulatory appendix.
Importable Goods: These goods are subject to specific declaration requirements when they fall under the classification of dangerous goods during the customs documentation process.

Cargo Declaration: The registration of a cargo declaration is mandated to follow specific automated and manual procedures based on the nature of the shipment and the entry point. The process ensures consistency between the general segment declaration and the relevant bills of lading or airway bills.

In cases where automated registration fails due to technical errors or data mismatches, customs authorities are empowered to verify and register declarations manually upon the application of the relevant agent.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: The system acts as the primary platform for the automated registration of cargo declarations. It performs validation checks to ensure consistency between general segments and specific transport documents.
Customs officials may intervene in the system to resolve data discrepancies or execute manual registrations when the automated process is unavailable or hindered by technical issues.
Bill of Lading: Master and House Bills of Lading are central to cargo declaration registration. A single shipment may correspond directly to a general segment, while more complex shipments involving multiple consignments require the filing of both Master and House Bills of Lading.
The registration of a cargo declaration is contingent upon the alignment and consistency of these documents with the general segment declaration.
Airway Bill: For cargo arriving via air, airlines or their agents must file Master Airway Bills and, where applicable, House Airway Bills into the customs system. These documents serve as the foundation for cargo registration at customs airports.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: Customs officials are responsible for resolving inconsistencies between declarations and transport documents upon a formal application from the declarant. They are also authorized to conduct manual registrations when the automated customs system cannot process a declaration.

processed_clauses.clause_title: কার্গো ঘোষণা সংশোধন ও সম্পূরক কার্গো ঘোষণা দাখিল

Person in Charge of Conveyance: This role, along with the owner or designated agent, is responsible for submitting applications for cargo declaration amendments or supplementary cargo declarations within a specified timeframe after registration.
They are required to provide necessary non-objection certificates and supporting documents when applying for cargo declaration amendments.
Customs Assessment: Any amendment request made after the completion of customs assessment is classified as a significant error and requires approval at a higher departmental level.
Serious errors identified in cargo declarations necessitate full physical inspection of goods to verify their value, origin, and classification before final customs assessment is completed.
Bill of Lading: Certain changes related to the type, nature code, or sender information on the bill of lading are categorized as clerical errors that can be processed at the Assistant or Deputy Commissioner level.
Changes involving the nature or type of the bill of lading require specific supporting documentation to be resolved.
Value: Applications to amend the value of goods declared in a cargo declaration must be handled with heightened caution and strict verification of supporting documents by the Commissioner of Customs.
A change in the value of a consignment is classified as a serious error requiring high-level administrative review.
Container: Errors involving container types, prefix numbers, sizes, or seal numbers are classified based on their complexity, with minor discrepancies treated as clerical errors and major ones as serious errors.
Specific changes, such as container size or status shifts, mandate distinct approval processes depending on whether they are classified as clerical or serious errors.
Consignee: The identification of the consignee and notify party, including their Business Identification Number, is subject to strict amendment rules where inaccuracies may be classified as either clerical or serious errors depending on the specific circumstances.
Business Identification Number: Any error related to the Business Identification Number of the consignee or notify party is treated as a serious error requiring approval from the head of the customs station.
Goods Description: Modifying the description of goods in a cargo declaration is considered a serious error and must be processed through the designated head of the customs station.

Customs Clearance: The submission and registration of cargo declarations allow importers or their authorized agents to proceed with formal declarations under the relevant legal provisions.
Consignments not selected for physical examination under risk management systems may be cleared immediately upon arrival, provided that all customs duties and taxes are paid.
Risk Management: Goods selected for physical inspection under risk management criteria must undergo mandatory examination and legal processing before release.
Clearance is prohibited for any shipment that is flagged for examination or for which credible intelligence information exists, regardless of its initial risk assessment status.
Customs Act 1969: The procedures for filing product declarations are governed by the requirements set forth in Section 81 of this Act.

Customs Act 2023: This clause provides specific provisions to facilitate the fulfillment of the objectives stated under Section 96 of the Customs Act 2023.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: For shipments where cargo declaration cannot be filed electronically as a single entry, the system allows for the submission of declarations based on transport documents like bills of lading, airway bills, or transport receipts.
The system may be used to uniquely flag shipments using specific import codes and is responsible for providing exit numbers and ensuring port release after data verification.
Except for shipments selected for physical inspection under risk management, the system facilitates the verification of declarations and the payment of duties and taxes for clearance.
Import Clearance: Clearance is granted for shipments based on transport documents when standard electronic cargo declaration is not feasible, provided the goods are not selected for physical examination under risk management.
Risk Management: Shipments are subjected to risk assessment, where physical examination remains mandatory for those selected by the system, while others may proceed based on the authenticity of the submitted declarations.
Import Duty: The clause stipulates that duties and taxes must be paid to enable the clearance of goods that have had their declarations and authenticity verified.

Customs Manifest: This document provides the standard structure for capturing general information, shipping details, transport data, and cargo specifics required for customs reporting.
It mandates the declaration of arrival and departure details, vessel information, and comprehensive totals for bills, packages, and containers to facilitate customs clearance.
Shipping Agent: The shipping agent is a required entity in the manifest, responsible for providing essential carrier and shipping information for the vessel's arrival or departure.
Container: The manifest requires detailed reporting of containerized cargo, including the total count of boxes and their corresponding gross weight to ensure accurate tracking.
Vessel: The manifest tracks vessel-specific information including name, nationality, registration number, IMO number, and tonnage to monitor transport assets during the clearance process.
Master of the Vessel: The master of the vessel is identified as a critical role for reporting, requiring their information to be captured within the transport section of the customs manifest.
Form: This document functions as the official form required under the customs rules for documenting the particulars of arrival and departure for commercial conveyances.

Manifest: This form captures comprehensive general information regarding the arrival and departure of conveyances, including voyage details and office codes.
It serves as the primary document for declaring cargo details, values, and transport status upon arrival or departure.
Shipping Agent: The form requires the identification of the carrier or shipping agent responsible for the transport operation.
Consignor: The document includes fields to record the details of the consignor or exporter for the goods being transported.
Consignee: The document includes fields to record the details of the importer or consignee responsible for the cargo.
Vessel: The document tracks vessel information including transport mode, name, nationality, and arrival/departure metrics.
Container: The document accounts for total container counts, package codes, and mark numbers associated with the shipment.
Goods Description: Detailed descriptions of goods, including weight, volume, and package status, must be declared on this form.
Value: The form captures declared values including freight amounts, customs value, insurance value, and transport costs for audit purposes.
Transit: The form includes specific sections to document transit movements and associated reference documentation.
Transshipment: The form includes specific sections to document transhipment movements and associated reference documentation.
Dangerous Goods: The form requires an indication of the dangerous goods status associated with the manifest items.

Car Pass: This document is a standardized form used to document and track the movement of vehicles crossing the border between India and Bangladesh.
It serves as an official record for customs authorities to endorse the entry and exit of commercial vehicles, including details on owners, drivers, goods, and associated shipping documentation.
Vehicle: The form requires comprehensive identification of the vehicle, including registration, engine, and chassis details, to facilitate cross-border monitoring.
It mandates documentation of the vehicle's movement, specifically tracking entries and returns for both Indian and Bangladeshi vehicles.
Goods: The car pass requires a description of the goods being transported, including invoice numbers, weight, and quantity, to ensure accurate customs declarations.
Importer: The form requires the identification and address of the importer to maintain a clear record of the receiving party for the transported goods.
Exporter: The form requires the identification and address of the exporter to maintain a clear record of the shipping party for the transported goods.
Bank: The car pass must include the letter of credit number and the details of the opening bank to verify the financial legitimacy of the trade transaction.

Form: This document provides a template for Form-K, which serves as a formal authorization for appointing an agent to handle customs declarations.
Vehicle and Cargo Declaration Submission: Rule 6(2) of these rules mandates the use of this specific form when authorizing an agent to submit declarations for conveyance and cargo.
Agent: The form facilitates the appointment of an agent who is authorized to submit declarations on behalf of the person in charge or owner of a conveyance.
Commissioner of Customs: The authorized form is addressed to the Commissioner of Customs or the Customs Station Chief of the relevant customs house or station.
Goods: The declaration form requires detailed information regarding the description, quantity, weight, and packaging of the goods being imported or transported.
Car Pass: A car pass is a required attachment that must accompany the authorization form during the declaration process.
Bank: The declaration must include financial details including the letter of credit number, opening date, and the name of the bank and branch associated with the transaction.
Importer: The form requires the submission of the name and address of the consignee or importer.
Exporter: The form requires the submission of the name and address of the consignor or exporter.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: This person or their designated operator is responsible for signing and submitting the authorization form to the customs authorities.

Cargo Declaration: This form serves as the official application for amending a cargo declaration or submitting a supplementary cargo declaration.
Applicants must provide detailed information about the transport, importer, exporter, and the specific nature of the goods being amended.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs or an authorized officer is the designated authority to receive and review applications for cargo declaration amendments.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the governing body responsible for issuing the official administrative orders and forms for customs procedures.
Customs Clearance: The application requires the user to disclose whether the goods have been examined, removed from the port of arrival, or if a bill of entry has already been filed, as these factors influence the amendment process.
